items.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 22 at 3:04PM PST until November 25 at 3:00AM PST by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
items.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor to moderate coastal
flooding is expected. For the Coastal Flood Watch, significant
coastal flooding is possible. Most susceptible time of flooding
will be around the time of the morning high tides between about
730 AM and 930 AM, especially Wednesday and Thursday.

* WHERE...Ventura County Beaches.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 3 AM Monday to 3
AM PST Wednesday. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from late
Tuesday night through Thursday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...There is the potential for damaging flooding of sea
water over some vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially
around the time of high tide, including over beaches, roads, and
structures including piers. Significant beach erosion is
possible. There is an increased risk for ocean drowning. Rip
currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Large
breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off beaches and
rocks, and capsize small boats near shore.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Highest risk likely Wednesday and
Thursday with potential for significant impacts. Elevated to
high surf is expected much of the week, with even the
possibility of warning- level surf at times from Wednesday
afternoon into Thursday. Additional products will likely be
needed into Friday.
items.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. Plan
for extra travel time as some roads may be closed.

items.headline: Marine Weather Statement issued November 22 at 2:21PM PST by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
items.description:
FRONTAL PASSAGE WILL BRING THE POTENTIAL FOR HEAVIER SHOWERS AND
ISOLATED THUNDERSTORMS TO THE COASTAL WATERS NOW THROUGH THIS
EVENING

A moist and unstable air mass will bring the potential for heavier
showers and isolated thunderstorms to the coastal waters. Any
thunderstorm or stronger shower that form will be capable of
producing locally gale force winds and rough seas, dangerous
lightning, heavy rainfall with reduced visibility, and a remote
risk of a waterspout.
